question: For $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\3&5\end{bmatrix}$, the matrix equation $AX=\begin{bmatrix}7\\18\end{bmatrix}$ has $X=\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\end{bmatrix}$. Using $A^{-1}$, find $2x-y$.
explanation:
Step 1: Check whether the inverse exists
The determinant of $A$ is $$|A|=(1)(5)-(2)(3)=-1\ne0$$ Hence, $A$ is invertible.
Step 2: Calculate the inverse
Using $A^{-1}=\frac{1}{|A|}\operatorname{adj}A$, $$A^{-1}=-\begin{bmatrix}5&-2\\-3&1\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-5&2\\3&-1\end{bmatrix}$$
Step 3: Determine $X$
Thus, $$X=A^{-1}B=\begin{bmatrix}-5&2\\3&-1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}7\\18\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1\\3\end{bmatrix}$$
Step 4: Find the required expression
Therefore, $$2x-y=2(1)-3=-1$$
